We recall 43, Def. 4.46] that a spacetime is future distinguishing if I† (p) = I (q) → p = q (and similarly in the past case). A spacetime is weakly distinguishing if I† (p) = I† (q) and I- (p) = I- (q) → p = q, cf. [13, Def. 4.47]. A spacetime is distinguishing if I† (p) = I† (g) or I-(p) = I- (q) → p = q, cf. 43, Def. 4.59. It is convenient to introduce the following notions

Definition 2.2. We say that the the Lorentzian distance future distinguishes events (the spacetime is future d-distinguishing) if dp = da → p = q, and that is past distinguishes events if d° = d' → p = q. The spacetime is ddistinguishing if it is both future and past d-distinguishing, namely: d' = d' or dp = da → p = q. We say that the spacetime is weakly d-distinguishing if d = d and dp = da → p = q. Note that d-distinction implies 'future or past d-distinction' which implies weak d-distinction. Remark 2.3. Weak d-distinction is called just d-distinction (or it is said that the Lorentzian distance distinguishes events) in 45, 13 as this is the only version that plays a role in those works.

Corollary 2.4. On a spacetime (M, 9) (future/past/weak) d-distinction is equivalent to (resp. future/past/weak) distinction.
